page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. Built without simultaneous multithreading, each core provides an isolated execution path supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and an aggregate 80 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning is set at 384.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for disk persistence.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core computational throughput and high memory bandwidth. Multi-threaded evaluations such as Geekbench multi-core (25,168.0), software compilation with Clang (74,635.0), and bzip3 decompression (557.87 GB/sec) score within the top tier. Memory subsystem operations achieve 344.68 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 152.46 GB/sec in large-block writes. Furthermore, database operations and static web serving yield top-tier figures, while single-core performance registers in the average to upper quartiles across Geekbench and stress-ng suites.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high compute density and extensive memory allocation without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware. The omission of bundled local NVMe storage requires external persistent disks, introducing an architectural dependency for I/O-intensive pipelines. The configuration is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, distributed databases, build automation clusters, and mid-tier LLM inference execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-48 is an Arm-based instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs on 48 physical ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 3.0 GHz. Accompanied by 384.0 GB of system memory, the machine delivers a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, complemented by an 80 MB L3 cache architecture. The configuration includes zero local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing persistent I/O via external network storage. Benchmark evaluations reflect exceptional multi-threaded performance, demonstrating top-tier results in Clang software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, and static web serving throughput reaching 104.03 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains robust with 344.68 GB/sec uncached read throughput. Providing high memory density and dedicated core allocation without hyperthreading contention, this instance is suited for memory-bound relational databases, large-scale Redis deployments, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized backend microservices.
